transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm doing this right, but my regular doctor actually told me I needed to come in. She says I've gotten a little too thin recently. 

I mean, I try to take good care of myself, but I guess... well, I do notice my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me lately when I'm doing my cleaning rounds at the building. So she's probably right to be a little concerned, don't you think? 

It's just... I'm a little embarrassed to admit this, and I really hope it doesn't sound terrible, but... part of me still feels a bit relieved when I see the number on the scale go lower. Is it okay that I said that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find yourself intentionally limiting how much you eat or avoiding certain foods because you're worried about gaining weight or because you want to lose more weight?

Well... I wouldn't say I'm completely avoiding food or anything drastic like that. I still make sure my family is well-fed. I always cook nice, full plates for my husband and my mother-in-law, you know? I want them to be healthy. 

But... I suppose, um... by the time I actually sit down with them, I usually just tell myself that I don't need all that much. Like, maybe just my coffee, or a few vegetables... or sometimes just half a piece of toast. I tell myself that's enough for me, especially since I'm on my feet so much at work. 

I just... I don't want to overdo it, you know? Is that... does that make sense? I hope that answers what you were asking.
Do you feel a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you're already at a low weight?

Well... I don't know if I'd use the word 'fear' exactly. That sounds so... serious, and I really don't want to make a big fuss out of nothing. But, um... I suppose I do get a little anxious about it. 

Like, if I happen to eat something a bit heavier, maybe some pasta or the biscuits I bake for my husband... I just, well, I spend the rest of the day feeling so scared that it's going to show on me right away. I'll catch myself checking my reflection in the glass doors when I'm sweeping the lobby, just... worrying. And then I start thinking I need to do extra rounds or scrub a little harder to make up for eating it. 

I know that probably sounds so silly for a woman my age to be worrying about things like that. I hope I'm not sounding too ridiculous... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you helpful answers.

When you look in the mirror or check your reflection, do you feel that you appear larger than you actually are, or do you feel that your concerns about your weight are more about staying healthy and fit?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't sound vain. I know at sixty-four I shouldn't be obsessing over my reflection, and I do want to be healthy, of course I do. But... 

It's just, when I look in the mirror and I see that I've stayed small and... neat, I guess... it just makes me feel like I'm handling everything right. Like I'm keeping everything under control. But if I look and my stomach seems even the least bit full, or if I feel like I look a little softer... I just feel this awful sense that I've let myself go. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I'm sorry if it's not the right way to think about it. I just... I like feeling tidy and put together. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you believe your current weight or shape has a strong impact on your self-worth or how you see yourself as a person?

Well... I suppose it does, a little bit. I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm shallow. I know there are much more important things in life than how I look, especially at my age, and I try so hard to be a good wife and a hard worker. 

But... yes, I guess it does affect how I feel about myself. Like I was saying before, when I look in the mirror and I see that I'm staying small and neat... it just makes me feel like I'm doing a good job. Like I'm keeping my life organized and handling everything the right way. It makes me feel capable, I suppose. 

But... if I happen to catch a glimpse of myself and my stomach looks even the least bit full, or if my clothes feel a tiny bit snug... I just feel this terrible wave of disappointment in myself. I feel like I've completely let myself go, like I'm failing somehow. 

I know that's probably not the right way to measure my worth, and I'm really sorry if that sounds foolish. I just... I like to feel like I'm doing things correctly. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick, take laxatives or diuretics, or exercise excessively to prevent weight gain?

Oh, no, no, I would never do anything like that. I mean, making myself sick or taking pills... that sounds so extreme, and I really wouldn't want to do anything to harm my body. I try very hard to be responsible. 

I do like to stay active, though. Like I mentioned, if I feel I've eaten a bit too much, I might just... well, I might scrub the floors a little harder or take the stairs a few extra times while I'm working. But it's just my job, you know? I'm a cleaner, so being on my feet and working hard is just part of what I do. It's not... excessive, I don't think. It's just being thorough. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong. Being a hard worker is a good thing, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm taking care of myself the right way.
Do you find that how you judge yourself or how you feel about yourself often depends on how you feel about your weight or the way you look?

I think... well, yes. It's very much like I was trying to say just a little bit ago, and I'm so sorry if I didn't explain it properly the first time. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. 

But yes, it really does. When I can see that I've stayed small and neat, I just feel like I'm handling everything right. It makes me feel like I'm a responsible person who has things in order. But if I catch my reflection and my stomach looks even the least bit full... I just get this awful, heavy feeling that I've completely let myself go. It really does change my whole view of myself for the day. 

I know it's probably silly for a woman my age to judge herself that way, and I try not to be superficial. I hope I'm not just repeating myself too much... did that answer your question okay?
Would you say that your overall sense of who you are and how you feel about yourself is often based on how you feel about your weight or your body shape?

Well... yes, I suppose it is. I... I know you just asked me something very similar, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same things over again. I'm trying so hard to give you the right answers. 

But yes, my weight and shape really do seem to be the main way I judge myself. It's like I mentioned... if I stay small and neat, I feel like a good, responsible person. I feel like I'm handling my life right. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the tiniest bit full, it just ruins everything. I feel like I've completely let myself go, like I'm a failure. 

I know it sounds so foolish for someone my age to care so much about that. I should be focused on being a good wife and doing my job well... and I do try, I really do. But that feeling about my body just takes over. I hope that makes sense? I'm so sorry if I'm just repeating myself.
Would you say that your weight or shape has been influencing your self-evaluation more than it should, to the point where it affects your daily life or how you feel about yourself overall?

Well... yes, I think it probably does. I'm so sorry, I know we're going over the same ground, and I really hope I'm not testing your patience. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to understand. 

But yes, it really does affect my whole day, maybe more than it should. Like I was saying, if I can just stay small and neat, I feel like I'm doing a good job... like I'm a responsible person who has everything under control. But then, if I happen to catch my reflection and my stomach looks even the least bit full, it just... it completely changes how I feel about myself. I just get this awful feeling that I've let myself go, and it's hard to shake that off while I'm trying to work or be around my husband. 

I know I shouldn't let it bother me so much. I try to focus on my cleaning and being useful, I really do. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm being helpful.
